Incorrect Word Numbers and Base/Root Words. I love to dive into the Greek and Hebrew words when I study the Bible. In particular I love to look at the specific Greek word used in the New Testament and find its root or base word. 

 Overall the electronic Strongs available here and attached to some paid Greek and Hebrew language Bible apps is good but has some errors.
So far I have found two with the latest one being in the word for Children (Τeknon - Tέκνον) found in Matthew 10:24. This electronic Strongs has the root as being number G5043 (Timoria - Τιμωρία) which means punishment! They say the root word is Timoria which according to this Strongs app means "a child that is produced". When you click on Timoria you get the word punishment. 

It's easy for me to find the Greek and Hebrew because I read both, but, for someone who doesn't, and who has no idea about two and three letter stems in words this could cause problems.

Two problems. 1. The search will bring up words within words. Search for “age” and message, marriage, bondage, advantage, etc. will be highlighted. 2. If one chooses one verse to find the definition of the word being searched for, and taps on that word in that verse, you are taken to another page where the definition can be accessed. But there’s no way to return to the word search to check definitions in other verses. Also, the definitions of words are often confusing and difficult to understand. Apparently, the definitions used are from the original Strong’s Concordance. Essential In All Study of Scripture. The Strong’s Concordance is an essential resource for understanding the Bible. Far too many Christians take Bible translations at face value, even though they know that the Bible was translated by a human. When people translate the Bible, they do so by giving their own interpretation. That doesn’t mean that they are wrong. What it does mean is that because there are so many ways to translate the ancient languages of the Bible into English, translators will transcribe what the Bible says in the way that they think best represents what the Bible says. But the truth is, no reader, of any translation can be absolutely confident in the representation that the translators provide. Especially as so many translators only represent the Bible as how their denomination wants you to understand it. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary for each reader to study the Bible from the original language as presented in the strong concordance.
 I would say it is even highly irresponsible on the part of the reader to not see what the Bible says for themselves in it’s original language. One cannot simply leave to chance what the God had spoken by trusting what someone else has transcribed. It is for this reason that so much of the Christian Church is Biblically illiterate or misguided. The Strong’s Concordance is your portal into understanding what God originally said in scripture. It is an invaluable resource and should not be neglected. I have used it for decades and I can’t tell you how often I’ve been blown away by what God has revealed to me in it and also by how many Bible teachers fail to understand the Bible correctly.
